name: Ezetimibe
summary: Selectively blocks intestinal cholesterol absorption, providing additive LDL lowering on top of statins with a distinct mechanism.
mechanism: Inhibits the NPC1L1 transporter at the intestinal brush border, reducing absorption of dietary and biliary cholesterol and lowering hepatic cholesterol delivery.
pharmacodynamics: Adds approximately 15–20% LDL lowering when combined with a statin.

pharmacokinetics.metabolism: Hepatic glucuronidation (UGT1A1, UGT1A3, UGT2B15); enterohepatic recirculation

safety.pregnancy: Limited human data; use only if clearly needed
safety.lactation: Caution (excreted in rat milk; human data lacking)
contraindications: With a statin: active liver disease (combination use)
warnings: Rare myopathy/rhabdomyolysis, mainly with statin combinations
monitoring: Liver enzymes if used with a statin

indications: Primary hyperlipidemia (alone or with a statin)
clinicalPearls: Dosing is fixed at 10 mg — no titration; works synergistically with statins.
Often combined with simvastatin or rosuvastatin in single-pill products.
good: Add-on LDL reduction in patients already on a statin or statin-intolerant.
bad: Modest efficacy as monotherapy; not a substitute for a potent statin.
